Introduction

This is a list of monsters in Dragon Quest 11 organised by region. It is based on the PS4 version, but the PC version is identical and so PC users should be able to use this too.

I have also added sections for the Switch version's 3D mode as well. This does not cover the 3DS version, nor Switch 2D mode.

Using this Guide

The monsters are in the order shown in the Defeated Monsters "By Region" section in-game. This can be accessed by pressing whichever button you have assigned to bring up the menu (this will be the triangle button on PS4), then selecting "Misc.", "Info", "Defeated Monster List", and "View Monsters by Region".

The tables will show common/rare item drops, EXP, and gold, as well as locations and special conditions. They will also have images showing what the monsters look like.

The regional bestiary order changes twice at major plot events. These story sections have been designated "Acts" by fans, so the regional list is divided into three acts. For completion's sake, there is also a separate section for bosses and enemies which don't appear on the regional list.

I have added Switch specific sections for the Switch's 3D mode and put the corresponding console platform in brackets in the title. Hopefully this is self-explanatory, but PS4 in brackets means the section applies to PS4, Switch means Switch, and PS4/Switch means it applies to both.

The ID numbers correspond to the PS4 version of the game at all times. I have kept them as such because it would break too many image links if I changed them at this point, plus it would simply be too confusing to have ID numbers for both PS4 and Switch when the same number can mean a different monster from each game. So, in this guide ID numbers 001-662 refer to the original PS4 monsters, while ID numbers 663-740 refer to the Switch additions.

With the exception of Tickington, I will not be covering 2D mode, for two reasons. One is time - I don't simply don't have it. Two, between the PS4 and Switch versions, I have spent over 400 hours on this game. I am burned out. At this point I don't have the inclination to go through what is going to be my sixth playthrough and get all the encounter data from all those random battles. If you want to collect that data yourself and post the info in a guide of your own, feel free to do so.

Regional Bestiary

Regional Bestiary Notes

Terminology

DAY/NIGHT: self-explanatory. If the monster only appears during the day, it will be marked with DAY. If it only appears at night, it will be marked with NIGHT.

Time will pass naturally as you go through areas. You can check the time of day by bringing up the area map and looking at the time-dial at the bottom of the screen. To quickly change the time of day, rest at a campsite or at an inn.

RAIN/SNOW: this monster only appears in rainy/snowy weather.

CLEAR: this monster only appears during clear weather conditions (i.e. no rain or snow).

In every area where the weather can change, you can find a weather cow who will tell you what the next day's weather is. If it is due to rain the next day at dawn, then you can rest at an inn/campsite until dawn to speed things up.

Here are the weather cow locations:

  1. Emerald Coast - western part of map, near where the two paths from the Heliodor Region meet. Forecasts rain/clear weather.
  2. The Manglegrove (1) - centre part of map, near the path that goes towards the broken Costa Valor bridge. Forecasts rain/clear weather.
  3. The Manglegrove (2) - southern part of map, southeast of the item vendor/east of the bridge. Forecasts rain/clear weather.
  4. Laguna di Gondolia - centre part of map, at the start/end of the wooden platform area. Forecasts rain/clear weather.
  5. Zwaardsrust Region - northeast of the ship's docking area (or alternatively, south of Warrior's Rest inn). Forecasts rain/clear weather.
  6. Dundrasil Region - by the tree to the east of the campsite. Forecasts rain/clear weather.
  7. Champs Sauvage Region - southern part of map, near the ruins west of Phnom Nonh. At the southeastern end of the ring-shaped body of water. Forecasts rain/clear weather.
  8. Sniflheim Region - eastern part of map, just east of the exit/entrance to Sniflheim City. Near where the horse bell is. Forecasts snow/clear weather.
  9. Snaerfelt Region - northwest of the campsite, amongst some trees. Forecasts snow/clear weather.

METAL SLIME: this refers to a metal slime type enemy. These monsters do not appear on the field map; they only appear in battle with other monsters. They are quite rare, have massive amounts of defence, and have a tendency to flee, but if you can defeat them before they escape they yield lots of EXP. The best way to defeat them is to use an ability which makes use of critical hits (e.g. Lightning Strike, Critical Claim) as critical hits ignore defence.

RAREFIED: this is a rare variant of a monster, which only appears in battle together with its more common variety; it does not appear on the field. You need to fight the common version over and over until the rare version appears. This can take a while depending on RNG.

There are two items which can increase the chances of finding these rare monsters:

  • Circle of Serendipity - hand in 75 medals at the Academie Des Medailles (Act 2)
  • Wings of Serendipity - win the Black Cup horse race on difficult (Act 3)

AMALGOOMATED: Later on in the game, the regular blue slime enemies will merge to become one large King Slime during battle. In order to get the Slime (Amalgoomated) entry, you must defeat the group of slimes before they merge.

??? - If this is in the map location column then it means I couldn't find the monster in the listed area. In these cases I offer an alternative location in the notes underneath the table.

Boss/Event: Bosses and some other scripted encounters do not show up on the regional bestiary. However I will list any bosses and additional encounters in or near the region separately underneath the table. This is so you can help keep track of which entries are added to the bestiary. To avoid spoilers I only list the ID no. of the boss enemy; for the full list of bosses with names, please look at the bosses section instead.

Mount: You can ride this monster. When out in the field, or in a dungeon, look out for a monster with yellow sparkles. Defeat it in battle, and you will be able to ride it. This allows you to access otherwise inaccessible areas.

Other Notes


  1. The listed order of enemies in the tables matches the order in the regional bestiary in the game, which can be different depending on the version of the game you're playing. It is for the most part chronological, but not always. I have kept the order to the game's order so that it's easier to cross-reference with the list in-game.
  2. If you miss a regular version of an enemy, you can still defeat the Vicious/Malicious version of the same enemy later on, and you'll automatically get the entry of the regular version as well. For example, the Brownie enemy can no longer be found in Act 3, but if you defeat the Malicious Brownie, you'll receive the entry for both the regular Brownie and the Malicious Brownie. Because of this, no entry is permanently missable.
  3. I only list one possible location for an enemy on the field map, which will be where I personally found it, but there may be other possible locations for each enemy as well.
  4. There is one dungeon which is NOT listed in the regional bestiary: Heliodor Castle (Act 2). For convenience I have listed the enemies that appear here as well, but note that there is no in-game regional list to compare it to; you'll have to keep track of which enemies you need to defeat yourself.
  5. Quests that require you to defeat a specific monster must be completed in the specified area. For example, if you are attempting the "Light It Up" quest, you must defeat the Brollygagger in the Champs Sauvage; it won't count if you try to defeat one in the Other Side dungeon.
